blocks.text: How do account executives get paid and manage income volatility

Your compensation as an account executive typically includes a base salary and a commission percentage. This structure means your total earnings vary based on your performance. Managing this requires a clear view of your pipeline and personal budget. You should treat your income like a business forecast. Use a simple spreadsheet to track your expected commission payouts against your fixed monthly expenses.
Why financial planning becomes a burden

Many account executives struggle with financial planning because they rely on manual processes. You likely spend time moving data between your CRM and your personal financial spreadsheets. This manual work leads to errors and takes time away from selling. Disconnected tools are another major cause of inefficiency. When your CRM does not talk to your planning app, you end up doing double the work.
Fixes for your financial planning routine

items: Use macOS Split View to keep your CRM and your budget spreadsheet side by side. Hover over the green button in the top left of any window to activate this.
Set up a recurring calendar event in Apple Calendar for your budget review. This ensures you do not forget to track your variable income.
Use 1Password to store your financial logins securely. This prevents you from wasting time resetting passwords during your planning sessions.
Create a standard folder in Finder for all your compensation plans and tax documents.

blocks.text: Using your Mac to optimize your workflow

Your Mac has built-in tools that help you manage your day. Use Command + Space to open Spotlight and launch your most used apps quickly. If you are working in a browser, use Command + T to open a new tab and Command + W to close it. These shortcuts save you time when you are juggling multiple client tasks.

faq.question: How can I better track my commission payouts?
faq.answer: Maintain a dedicated spreadsheet where you log every closed deal and the expected commission date. Review this against your bank statement monthly.
